speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: asked the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs (a) what benchmarks and targets has the Ministry set for road traffic fatality rates; and (b) what additional measures are being contemplated to address the rise in accidents and casualties involving motorcyclists and pillion riders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Ultimately, whether these measures succeed depend on all our road users.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In terms of benchmarks and targets in all of these areas, whether relating to crime, or to accidents, or other matters as such, the Government must approach on the basis that there is zero tolerance and that we should aim to prevent such accidents completely.
But we should also be realistic to accept that in any society, there will be crime.
In every society, there will be accidents, and there will be other such incidents going forward.
Some people will get into accidents, commit crime, regardless of the penalties.
And attempts to prevent them from doing so, will not deter some.
This will reduce the risk of skidding and maintain vehicle stability during sudden and hard braking.
TP also runs public education campaigns targeted at the riding community.
These campaigns overall encourage motorcyclists to adopt safe riding habits and don protective riding gear.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Just one supplementary question for the Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I understand from the latest mid-year traffic situation report that the number of speeding-related accidents has declined.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: But at the same time, the number of accidents involving motorcyclists have still risen by close to about 10% year-on-year, in the first half of the year.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The ABS requirement from 2027 onwards is a welcome addition.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: At the same time, will the Minister of State be able to share, based on his analysis of past motorcycle accidents, what are some of the key reasons for these accidents and fatalities, and any other preventive measures that the TP is considering implementing?

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Speaker, I thank the Member for his supplementary question.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: So, it is an area of concern for us and we do want to keep our motorcyclists, our riders safe.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: A whole series of measures are in place.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Both the Ministry of Home Affairs as well as our TP colleagues have been working very hard, be it from the aspect of public education, going upstream; be it in terms of licensing; be it in terms of penalties downstream; be it in terms of putting in place reminders on the roads, reminder messages in terms of getting people to pay attention to the speed, to ride safe and be considerate, for example, as well as enforcement measures on the streets, we have put in all the measures that we think are effective.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: As I mentioned in my earlier response, some of these measures are effective, but there will still be accidents that will take place.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: We will continue to review whether there are new technologies available in the market for us to adopt.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: I welcome the Member to share if there are other suggestions.
